title: Add TREY C SECURITY anti-abuse protections and expand the admin panel with security + management tools

requirements.text: Implement a backend anti-abuse/anti-DDoS protection layer branded as "TREY C SECURITY" that rate-limits and blocks abusive callers in a way compatible with Internet Computer constraints (no IP address access), applying protections to all update calls that mutate state (e.g., createOrder, updateOrderStatus, setTrackingNumber, deleteOrder, resetAllData, saveCallerUserProfile).

quotes: Add a super advanced Anti ddos system ... call the security system TREY C SECURITY

acceptanceCriteria: Backend enforces configurable per-caller throttling (e.g., per Principal) for protected update methods and rejects requests that exceed limits with a clear error message mentioning TREY C SECURITY.
Backend supports an admin-managed blocklist/allowlist for Principals, where blocked principals are denied access to protected endpoints.
Rate-limit state and blocklist persist across upgrades (use stable storage); if existing stable state format changes, add/adjust migration logic accordingly (only if needed).
All admin-only methods remain admin-only; protections do not weaken existing authorization checks.

requirements.text: Add backend TREY C SECURITY observability endpoints for administrators to view security posture: aggregated counters (allowed/denied/throttled), recent security events, and current configuration (rate-limit parameters, blocklist/allowlist sizes), all admin-gated.

quotes: make the admin panel more advanced as well every single thing you think it needs add it

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes admin-only methods to fetch security metrics and recent events suitable for rendering in the admin UI.
Security events include at least: timestamp, caller Principal, action/method name, decision (allowed/throttled/blocked), and reason.
Non-admin callers cannot access any TREY C SECURITY metrics/config endpoints (must trap/deny).

requirements.text: Add backend TREY C SECURITY administrative controls for tuning and response: enable/disable protections, update rate-limit thresholds, clear/reset security counters, and add/remove principals from blocklist/allowlist, all admin-gated and auditable.

quotes: make the admin panel more advanced as well every single thing you think it needs add it

acceptanceCriteria: Admin-only backend methods exist to update security configuration and to manage blocklist/allowlist entries.
Admin actions that change security configuration are recorded in the security event log (or a dedicated admin audit log) with timestamp and admin Principal.
Attempting to call these methods as a non-admin is denied.

requirements.text: Upgrade the frontend admin experience into a more advanced panel by adding a dedicated "TREY C SECURITY" section within the existing AdminPanelPage, showing security metrics, recent security events, and controls to manage protections (toggle, thresholds, blocklist/allowlist management).

quotes: make the admin panel more advanced as well ... call the security system TREY C SECURITY

acceptanceCriteria: Admin panel includes a clearly labeled "TREY C SECURITY" area (tab/section) using the existing cyber admin theme styles.

The security area renders: (1) KPI cards/counters, (2) a recent-events table/list, (3) blocklist/allowlist management UI, and (4) configuration controls; all wired to backend endpoints via React Query hooks.
All security actions show success/error toasts and update the displayed data via query invalidation/refetch.
Non-admin users still cannot access the admin panel (AdminGate behavior unchanged).

requirements.text: Make the admin panel "more advanced" by adding high-value admin tools beyond the current order list: bulk order actions (approve/ship/delete), data export (CSV download) for orders, and an admin audit log view for critical admin actions (e.g., resets, deletes, security config changes).

quotes: make the admin panel more advanced as well every single thing you think it needs add it

acceptanceCriteria: Admin can select multiple orders and apply bulk actions with confirmation prompts; UI clearly shows progress and per-action outcomes.
Admin can export the currently filtered order list to a CSV file from the UI (frontend-generated CSV is acceptable).
Backend records critical admin actions in an audit log that is admin-readable; admin panel provides a view to browse/filter recent audit entries.
Existing single-order actions continue to work as before.

constraints: Backend must remain a single-actor Motoko canister; keep all logic in backend/main.mo (single-actor architecture).
Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui (compose existing shadcn components instead).
Do not modify immutable frontend hook files listed by the platform (e.g., frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts(x), frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx).
Anti-DDoS protections must not depend on client IP addresses or third-party services; use Internet Computer-compatible signals (e.g., Principal/call patterns) only.
nonGoals: Implementing network-level DDoS mitigation outside the canister (e.g., CDN/WAF, IP-based blocking).
Adding third-party authentication providers (only Internet Identity is supported).
Real-time features (websockets/push notifications) for security events.
